addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# DocRED LoRA fine-tuned model evaluation: unconstrained + constrained (full_s1)
# Models: Qwen3-8B LoRA DocRED, Llama-3.1-8B LoRA DocRED
# Usage: bash scripts/run_docred_lora_eval.sh {qwen_unconstrained|qwen_constrained|llama_unconstrained|llama_constrained|all}

set -euo pipefail

source /root/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate base

cd /root/schema_semantic_constrained_ie

# --- Paths ---
QWEN_MODEL="/root/autodl-tmp/checkpoints/qwen_lora_docred_merged"
LLAMA_MODEL="/root/autodl-tmp/checkpoints/llama_lora_docred_merged"
DATA_PATH="data/docred/dev.json"
CONSTRAINTS_PATH="data/docred/ontology_constraints_docred.json"
MAX_NEW_TOKENS=4096
BATCH_SIZE=1

run_qwen_unconstrained() {
    echo "=== Qwen3-8B DocRED LoRA: unconstrained ==="
    python run_constrained_extraction.py \
        --mode unconstrained \
        --dataset docred \
        --model_path "$QWEN_MODEL" \
        --data_path "$DATA_PATH" \
        --constraints_path "$CONSTRAINTS_PATH" \
        --output_path outputs/w5_qwen_docred_lora_unconstrained_eval.jsonl \
        --device cuda:1 \
        --max_new_tokens $MAX_NEW_TOKENS \
        --batch_size $BATCH_SIZE
}

run_qwen_constrained() {
    echo "=== Qwen3-8B DocRED LoRA: constrained (full_s1) ==="
    python run_constrained_extraction.py \
        --mode full_s1 \
        --dataset docred \
        --model_path "$QWEN_MODEL" \
        --data_path "$DATA_PATH" \
        --constraints_path "$CONSTRAINTS_PATH" \
        --output_path outputs/w5_qwen_docred_lora_constrained_eval.jsonl \
        --device cuda:1 \
        --max_new_tokens $MAX_NEW_TOKENS \
        --batch_size $BATCH_SIZE
}

run_llama_unconstrained() {
    echo "=== Llama-3.1-8B DocRED LoRA: unconstrained ==="
    python run_constrained_extraction.py \
        --mode unconstrained \
        --dataset docred \
        --model_path "$LLAMA_MODEL" \
        --data_path "$DATA_PATH" \
        --constraints_path "$CONSTRAINTS_PATH" \

{"success": true, "data": {"stdout": "% Section 5 — Composability with Fine-Tuned Models
% exp_ids: w5_lora_scierc_unconstrained_eval, w5_lora_scierc_constrained_eval,
%          w5_llama_lora_scierc_unconstrained_eval, w5_llama_lora_scierc_constrained_eval

\subsection{Composability with Fine-Tuned Models}
\label{sec:composability-ft}

The cross-model validation in \S\ref{sec:cross-model} establishes that
OntoCoDec generalizes across model families in the zero-shot regime.
A complementary question is whether the same constraints remain useful
after task-specific fine-tuning, where the model has been trained to
emit ontology-conformant outputs and one might expect violations to
disappear on their own.
We test this by LoRA fine-tuning both Qwen3-8B and Llama-3.1-8B on
SciERC and then evaluating each fine-tuned model with and without the
two-layer constraints, yielding a 2$\times$2 design per model family.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3.4pt}
\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{@{}lll rr rr@{}}
\toprule
& & & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{Viol.~(\%)}}
& \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{F1}} \\
\cmidrule(lr){4-5} \cmidrule(l){6-7}
\textbf{Model} & \textbf{Train} & \textbf{Decode}
  & DR\,$\downarrow$ & CF
  & Rel.\,$\uparrow$ & Ent.\,$\uparrow$ \\
\midrule
\multirow{4}{*}{Qwen3-8B}
  & Zero-shot & U   & 15.37 & 0.08 & 8.23 & 31.01 \\
  & Zero-shot & S1  & \textbf{0.93}  & 9.90 & 8.36 & 30.98 \\
  & LoRA      & U   &  1.95 & 0    & 43.86 & 67.05 \\
  & LoRA      & S1  & \textbf{0.00}  & 1.18 & 43.77 & 67.05 \\
\midrule
\multirow{4}{*}{Llama-3.1-8B}
  & Zero-shot & U   & 13.34 & 0.24 & 2.68 & 23.56 \\
  & Zero-shot & S1  & \textbf{0.08} & 6.56 & 2.54 & 23.49 \\
  & LoRA      & U   &  1.11 & 0    & 45.45 & 67.76 \\
  & LoRA      & S1  & \textbf{0.09} & 0.46 & 45.47 & 67.76 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}}%
\caption{Composability with fine-tuning on SciERC (551 documents).
U: unconstrained; S1: full two-layer decoding.
LoRA $r{=}16$, $\alpha{=}32$, all-linear targets, 3 epochs, effective batch 16.
F1 $\times$100. RV and ET are 0\,\% in every constrained row and are
omitted for space.}
\label{tab:composability}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Fine-tuning does not eliminate ontology violations.}
LoRA fine-tuning lifts relation F1 from 8.23 to 43.86 (Qwen) and from
2.68 to 45.45 (Llama)---a 35--43\,pp gain that brings both models well
above the zero-shot regime.
% w5_lora_scierc_unconstrained_eval: R-F1=0.4386; w5_llama_lora_scierc_unconstrained_eval: R-F1=0.4545
Yet residual domain/range violations persist at 1.95\,\% (Qwen) and
1.11\,\% (Llama), and per-relation analysis shows tight-constraint
relations remain problematic: Evaluate-for retains 13.1\,\% DR for the
fine-tuned Qwen model despite achieving zero on six of the other seven
relations.
% w5_lora_scierc_unconstrained_eval.notes: Evaluate-for DR=13.13%
This pattern matches the tightness-driven mechanism of
\S\ref{sec:method}: relations whose valid type pairs cover a small
fraction of $|\mathcal{T}|^2$ resist coverage even at the data
distribution level, because the long tail of contexts is unlikely to
be exercised during fine-tuning.

\paragraph{Constraints compose with fine-tuning at no F1 cost.}
Applying full S1 decoding on top of the fine-tuned models eliminates
residual DR almost entirely (Qwen 1.95\%\,$\to$\,0.00\%, Llama
1.11\%\,$\to$\,0.09\%) while relation F1 changes by less than 0.1\,pp
($-$0.09\,pp Qwen, $+$0.02\,pp Llama) and entity F1 is identical to
the fine-tuned unconstrained baseline in both cases.
% w5_lora_scierc_constrained_eval: DR=0, R-F1=0.4377, E-F1=0.6705 (vs U: 0.4386, 0.6705)
% w5_llama_lora_scierc_constrained_eval: DR=0.0009, R-F1=0.4547, E-F1=0.6776 (vs U: 0.4545, 0.6776)
The fine-tuned model has already moved its output distribution away
from gross violations, so the constraint mask only intervenes on the
small residual mass; the cost of that intervention is negligible.
The CF rate at the fine-tuned regime is also markedly lower than at
zero-shot (1.18\,\% Qwen, 0.46\,\% Llama vs.\ 9.90\,\% and 6.56\,\%),
consistent with our analysis that CF reflects semantic ambiguity in
borderline assignments: fine-tuned models commit to more confident
type predictions, leaving fewer borderline cases for the per-relation
mask to flip.

\paragraph{Implication.}
Fine-tuning and decoding-time enforcement are complementary, not
substitutable.
Fine-tuning is the primary lever for extraction \emph{quality} (F1),
while constrained decoding is the primary lever for ontology
\emph{compliance} at the long tail.
A practitioner who fine-tunes for F1 still needs constraint
enforcement to deliver per-instance type validity, because the
relations with tightest constraints---those most important to enforce

{"success": true, "data": {"stdout": "#!/bin/bash
# DocRED LoRA fine-tuned model evaluation: unconstrained + constrained (full_s1)
# Models: Qwen3-8B LoRA DocRED, Llama-3.1-8B LoRA DocRED
# Usage: bash scripts/run_docred_lora_eval.sh {qwen_unconstrained|qwen_constrained|llama_unconstrained|llama_constrained|all}

set -euo pipefail

source /root/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate base

cd /root/schema_semantic_constrained_ie

# --- Paths ---
QWEN_MODEL="/root/autodl-tmp/checkpoints/qwen_lora_docred_merged"
LLAMA_MODEL="/root/autodl-tmp/checkpoints/llama_lora_docred_merged"
DATA_PATH="data/docred/dev.json"
CONSTRAINTS_PATH="data/docred/ontology_constraints_docred.json"
MAX_NEW_TOKENS=4096
BATCH_SIZE=1

run_qwen_unconstrained() {
    echo "=== Qwen3-8B DocRED LoRA: unconstrained ==="
    python run_constrained_extraction.py \
        --mode unconstrained \
        --dataset docred \
        --model_path "$QWEN_MODEL" \
        --data_path "$DATA_PATH" \
        --constraints_path "$CONSTRAINTS_PATH" \
        --output_path outputs/w5_qwen_docred_lora_unconstrained_eval.jsonl \
        --device cuda:1 \
        --max_new_tokens $MAX_NEW_TOKENS \
        --batch_size $BATCH_SIZE
}

run_qwen_constrained() {
    echo "=== Qwen3-8B DocRED LoRA: constrained (full_s1) ==="
    python run_constrained_extraction.py \
        --mode full_s1 \
        --dataset docred \
        --model_path "$QWEN_MODEL" \
        --data_path "$DATA_PATH" \
        --constraints_path "$CONSTRAINTS_PATH" \
        --output_path outputs/w5_qwen_docred_lora_constrained_eval.jsonl \
        --device cuda:1 \
        --max_new_tokens $MAX_NEW_TOKENS \
        --batch_size $BATCH_SIZE
}

run_llama_unconstrained() {
    echo "=== Llama-3.1-8B DocRED LoRA: unconstrained ==="
    python run_constrained_extraction.py \
        --mode unconstrained \
        --dataset docred \
        --model_path "$LLAMA_MODEL" \
        --data_path "$DATA_PATH" \
        --constraints_path "$CONSTRAINTS_PATH" \
        --output_path outputs/w5_llama_docred_lora_unconstrained_eval.jsonl \
        --device cuda:0 \
        --max_new_tokens $MAX_NEW_TOKENS \
        --batch_size $BATCH_SIZE
}

run_llama_constrained() {
    echo "=== Llama-3.1-8B DocRED LoRA: constrained (full_s1) ==="
    python run_constrained_extraction.py \
        --mode full_s1 \
        --dataset docred \
        --model_path "$LLAMA_MODEL" \
        --data_path "$DATA_PATH" \
        --constraints_path "$CONSTRAINTS_PATH" \
        --output_path outputs/w5_llama_docred_lora_constrained_eval.jsonl \
        --device cuda:0 \
        --max_new_tokens $MAX_NEW_TOKENS \
        --batch_size $BATCH_SIZE
}

case "${1:-all}" in
    qwen_unconstrained)   run_qwen_unconstrained ;;
    qwen_constrained)     run_qwen_constrained ;;
    llama_unconstrained)  run_llama_unconstrained ;;
    llama_constrained)    run_llama_constrained ;;
    all)
        run_qwen_unconstrained
        run_qwen_constrained
        run_llama_unconstrained
        run_llama_constrained
        ;;
    *)
        echo "Usage: $0 {qwen_unconstrained|qwen_constrained|llama_unconstrained|llama_constrained|all}"
        exit 1
        ;;
esac
